hindbrain.","printedPage":270,"pdfPage":288,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":119},{"text":"( Paradoxical means “apparently .","printedPage":274,"pdfPage":292,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":48},{"text":"The hypothalamus has both neurons that promote wakefulness and .","printedPage":277,"pdfPage":295,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":79},{"text":"Sleep apnea is often related to obesity, especially in middle-aged Most people in a coma either die or begin to recover within a few weeks.","One step up from a coma is a condition previously known as a vegetative state, now preferably called","Breathing is more regular, and a painful stimulus increases heart rate, breathing, and sweating.","Brain death is a condition with no sign of brain activity and no response to any stimulus. Physicians usually wait until someone has exhibited no sign of brain activity for 24 hours before pronouncing brain death, at which point most people believe it is ethical to remove life support.","Researchers did not even suspect that sleep has stages until they accidentally measured them, using an electroencephalograph (EEG) that records the average electrical activity near each electrode on the scalp (Figure 8.10).","During this period, stage 1 sleep, the EEG is dominated by irregular, jagged, low-voltage waves.","Brain activity is less than in relaxed wakefulness but higher than in other sleep stages. Because most neurons are out of phase with one another, the EEG is full of short, rapid, choppy waves.","A K-complex is a sharp wave associated with temporary inhibition of neuronal firing.","A sleep spindle is a burst of 12- to 14-Hz waves for at least half a second.","Sleep spindles result from oscillating interactions between cells in the thalamus and the cortex. During slow-wave sleep, heart rate, breathing rate, and brain activity decrease, while slow, large-amplitude waves increase (Figures 8.11d and e).","He noticed that during certain periods of apparent sleep, the cats’ brain activity was relatively high, but their neck muscles were completely relaxed.","After someone fell asleep, they turned the machine off, because the recording paper was expensive (before the days of computers), and they did not expect to observe anything interesting in the middle of the night anyway.","When they occasionally turned on the machine during the night and found evidence of eye movements, they at first assumed that something was wrong with the machine. They called these periods rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, and they soon realized that REM sleep was synonymous with what Jouvet called paradoxical sleep.","Researchers mostly use the term REM sleep, but they often prefer the term paradoxical sleep for species that lack eye movements.","During REM sleep, the EEG shows irregular, low-voltage fast waves that indicate increased neuronal activity.","However, during REM sleep, cells in the pons and medulla inhibit movement of the postural muscles, including those that support the head. Later research, however, found that people awakened during non-REM sleep sometimes report dreams also.","Any animal needs to regulate its level of alertness appropriate to the situation.","Many brain areas participate in the control of sleep and wakefulness.","After a cut through the midbrain separates the forebrain and part of the midbrain from lower structures, an animal enters prolonged sleep for the next few days. We might suppose that the animal sleeps just because the cut isolated the brain from sensory stimuli.","However, if a researcher cuts each individual tract that enters the medulla and spinal cord, thus depriving the midbrain of the sensory input, the animal still has normal periods of wakefulness and sleep.","A cut through the midbrain decreases arousal by damaging the reticular formation, a structure that extends from the medulla into the forebrain.","Some neurons of the reticular formation have axons ascending into the brain, and some have axons descending into the spinal cord. Magoun proposed that the reticular formation neurons with ascending axons are well suited to regulate arousal.","After a cut through the midbrain separates the forebrain and part of the midbrain from lower structures, an animal enters prolonged sleep for the next few days.","We might suppose that the animal sleeps just because the cut isolated the brain from sensory stimuli.","However, if a researcher cuts each individual tract that enters the medulla and spinal cord, thus depriving the midbrain of the sensory input, the animal still has normal periods of wakefulness and sleep. A cut through the midbrain decreases arousal by damaging the reticular formation, a structure that extends from the medulla into the forebrain.","Some neurons of the reticular formation have axons ascending into the brain, and some have axons descending into the spinal cord.","Magoun proposed that the reticular formation neurons with ascending axons are well suited to regulate arousal.","Axons from some of the cells release GABA, which inhibits behavior and promotes slow-wave sleep. Output from the locus coeruleus increases what engineers call “gain.” It increases the activity of the most active neurons and decreases the activity of less active neurons, enhancing attention to important information.","The hypothalamus has both neurons that promote wakefulness and neurons that promote sleep. Staying awake depends on orexin, especially toward the end of the day.","Other pathways from the lateral hypothalamus regulate cells in the basal forebrain (an area just anterior and dorsal to the hypothalamus).","During sleep, neurons in the thalamus become hyperpolarized, decreasing their response to stimuli and decreasing the information they send the cortex.","The brain responds to speech, especially by an unfamiliar voice, probably because it seems more dangerous than a familiar voice.","During sleep, neurons continue firing at only a bit less than their usual spontaneous rate. During sleep, axons from the pons and midbrain increase their release of GABA, inhibiting the synaptic spread of information from one neuron to another.","Because sleep depends on GABA-mediated inhibition, sleep can be local within the brain.","Brain areas usually wake up or go to sleep at nearly the same time, but not always.","Sleepwalkers generally have their eyes open, they orient to the world enough to find their way around, and they often remember some of what they did while sleepwalking, but they are confused and vulnerable, because most of the brain is not alert enough to process information and make reasonable decisions. During REM sleep, cells in the pons and medulla send messages that inhibit the spinal neurons controlling the arm and leg muscles.","The mutant gene increases their need for sleep.","The average adult human needs 71⁄2 to 81⁄2 hours of sleep per night, but some have been known to do well with as little as 3 hours per night.","Researchers have found families in which several people share a mutation causing them to average less than 6 hours per night.","Most of them consider their condition an advantage, and they do not suffer memory problems or any of the other complaints people usually experience after sleep deprivation. It also magnifies unpleasant emotional reactions and increases the risk of depression.","Insomnia can also be the result of epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, brain tumors, depression, anxiety, or other neurological or psychiatric conditions.","Some children suffer insomnia because they are milk-intolerant, and their parents, not realizing the intolerance, give them milk to drink right before bedtime.","One man suffered insomnia until he realized that he dreaded going to sleep because he hated waking up to go jogging. Frequent use causes dependence and an inability to sleep without the pills.","Ordinarily that delay causes problems, although it might help combat jet lag after traveling west.","One type of insomnia is sleep apnea, impaired ability to breathe while sleeping.","People with sleep apnea have breathless periods of a minute or so from which they awaken gasping for breath.","They may not remember their awakenings, although they certainly notice the consequences, such as sleepiness and impaired attention the following day. Prolonged sleep apnea leads to a loss of neurons, with an impairment of learning and other functions.","People with sleep apnea are advised to lose weight and avoid alcohol and tranquilizers (which relax the breathing muscles).","The most common treatment is a mask that covers the nose and delivers air under enough pressure to keep the breathing passages open (Figure 8.18). That procedure improves sleep and blood pressure, but it only slightly decreases the risk of stroke or heart attack, probably because many people continue to be overweight.","Narcolepsy, a condition characterized by periods of sudden sleepiness during the day, affects about 1 person in 1,000.","The H1N1 flu virus in 2009–2010 caused many cases of narcolepsy by strongly activating the immune system.","Narcolepsy is unique among behavioral disorders as it is the only one linked to a biochemical marker (low orexin levels) that is reliable enough to establish the diagnosis. Why REM? Why Dreams?","kind":"detailed_source_grounded_notes","printedStart":281,"printedEnd":290,"pdfStart":299,"pdfEnd":308,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sleep serves more than one proposed function, including energy conservation and contributions to memory. Different species show different patterns, providing clues about the constraints shaping sleep."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The module compares proposals about the functions of REM sleep and the origins of dreams, including activation-synthesis and neurocognitive views. Notice what each theory explains and what questions remain."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m8-3-study-1","text":"Why organisms sleep"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sleep is widespread across species, but its duration, posture, and organization differ considerably. Proposed functions include conserving energy, supporting restoration and regulation, and contributing to learning and memory. Evidence does not require sleep to have exactly one benefit for every species. Evolution may have added several functions to an older biological pattern. The important task is to compare predictions of different explanations rather than treating one appealing story as final."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m8-3-study-2","text":"Sleep and memory"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Some kinds of learning benefit from periods of sleep after practice. Sleep may influence stabilization, reorganization, or selective retention of information. These findings do not mean every memory is stored only during sleep or that extra sleep guarantees perfect learning. Study the difference between observing that sleep improves performance and establishing which sleeping brain events produce the benefit."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m8-3-study-3","text":"REM sleep and dreams"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"REM sleep has distinctive patterns of activity and muscle inhibition. The function of REM remains debated, and findings from deprivation and cross-species comparisons need cautious interpretation. The activation-synthesis hypothesis emphasizes how the brain interprets internally generated activity; neurocognitive approaches consider ongoing cognitive networks and the organization of dream experience. Both attempt to explain dreams through brain processes but differ in emphasis."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m8-3-study-4","text":"An evidence-based conclusion"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sleep, REM, and dreaming are related phenomena but should not be collapsed into a single question. A useful revision answer separates the function of sleep overall, the specific role of REM physiology, and the origin or meaning of dream experiences. The textbook emphasizes the limits of current understanding, so a strong answer presents hypotheses as hypotheses rather than universal facts."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h01","text":"Functions of Sleep"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"During sleep, we rest our muscles and decrease metabolism.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Fluid drains from the brain and spinal cord into the subarachnoid space, removing potentially harmful proteins and waste products .","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People who don’t get enough sleep react more severely than average to stressful events .","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Inadequate sleep is a major cause of accidents by workers and poor performance by college students.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Driving while sleep deprived is comparable to driving under the influence of alcohol .","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Even one night of sleeplessness activates the immune system, as if you were ill .","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h02","text":"Sleep and Energy Conservation"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Even if we agreed on what is the most important function of sleep for humans today, it might not be the function for which sleep originally evolved.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"All of those are valuable functions, but the original purpose of computers was to do mathematical calculations.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Similarly, sleep probably started with a simple function to which evolution added others later.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A likely hypothesis is that sleep’s original function, and still an important one, is to save energy .","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sleep conserves energy during the times when activity would be ineffective and possibly dangerous.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When NASA built the Rover spacecraft to explore Mars, they included a mechanism to make it “sleep” at night to conserve the batteries.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"During sleep, a mammal’s body temperature decreases by 1° or 2° C, enough to save a noticeable amount of energy.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Animals increase their sleep duration during food shortages, when energy conservation is especially important .","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h03","text":"Analogous to Sleep: Hibernation"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Hibernating animals decrease their body temperature, usually maintaining it just slightly above that of the environment, but always warm enough to prevent the blood from freezing.","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Heart rate and brain activity drop to almost nothing, neuron cell bodies shrink, and many synapses disappear, regenerating at the end of hibernation .","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Here are a few curious facts about hibernation:","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h04","text":"Species Differences in Sleep"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If one of the main functions of sleep is to decrease activity at times of relative inefficiency, we might expect to find little or no sleep in species that are equally effective at all times of day.","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In contrast to the fish in normal waters, which average more than 13 hours of sleep per day, the populations in caves have only 2 to 4 hours of sleep per day without a circadian rhythm .","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many animals that live near the North or South Pole greatly decrease their sleep during summer, when the sun is constantly above the horizon.","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Two elephant matriarchs, who take charge of protecting their troops, were observed to sleep two hours or less per night .","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"To do so, they evolved the ability to sleep on one side of the brain at a time.","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"These large birds never land on the water, because their feathers would become waterlogged and prevent them from taking flight again.","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"EEG records indicate that they have periods of slow-wave sleep in one hemisphere at a time, and REM periods in both hemispheres.","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Exactly how a mother dolphin, elephant matriarch, great frigate bird, or migratory bird decreases its sleep need is unknown, but the fact that it is possible fits with the idea that sleep is largely a way to conserve energy, and that the other functions of sleep can be performed briefly.","sourcePrintedPage":283,"sourcePdfPage":301,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Animals that need to be on the alert for predators get little sleep, whereas the predators themselves sleep easily.","sourcePrintedPage":283,"sourcePdfPage":301,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h05","text":"Sleep and Memory"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In contrast, if you learn something and then go to sleep, even a nap, your memory solidifies and may become better than it was before sleep .","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Another study found that a nap that included REM sleep enhanced performance on certain kinds of creative problem solving .","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Both REM sleep and slow-wave sleep have been linked to strengthening of memories .","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers recorded activity in the hippocampus during learning, and then recorded from the same locations during sleep, using microelectrodes within cells for laboratory animals and electrodes on the scalp for humans.","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The results: Patterns that occurred during sleep resembled those that had occurred during learning, except that they were more rapid during sleep.","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As the brain replays its experiences during sleep it forms new dendritic branches that strengthen the memories .","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Knowledge storage depends on highly synchronized sharp wave ripples that transfer information from the hippocampus","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An important way for sleep to strengthen memory is by weeding out the less successful connections.","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Research by Gina Poe and others has found that the brain conditions during sleep are ideal for pruning ineffective synapses and deleting unimportant memories .","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h06","text":"Functions of REM Sleep"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"On average, people spend about a third of their life asleep and about a fifth of sleep in REM, totaling about 600 hours of REM per year.","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One way to approach this question is to compare the people or animals with more REM to those with less.","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"REM sleep is widespread in mammals and birds, indicating that it is part of our ancient evolutionary heritage.","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As a rule, the species with the most total sleep hours also have the highest percentage of REM sleep .","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Cats spend up to 16 hours a day sleeping, much or most of it in REM sleep.","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, although memory consolidation does occur during REM, many people take antidepressant drugs that severely decrease REM sleep without causing memory problems .","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"During sleep, because they are shielded from the air, they deteriorate slightly .","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"According to this view, REM is a way of arousing a sleeper just enough to shake the eyes back and forth, and the other manifestations of REM are just by-products.","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"This idea makes sense of the fact that REM occurs mostly toward the end of the night’s sleep, when the fluid behind the eyes would be the most stagnant.","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h07","text":"Biological Perspectives on Dreaming"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Dream research faces a special problem: All we know about dreams comes from people’s self-reports.","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"We forget most dreams, and even when we do remember them, the details fade quickly.","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A common research procedure is to awaken people and ask for an immediate dream report.","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h08","text":"The Activation-Synthesis Hypothesis"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"According to the activation-synthesis hypothesis , a dream represents the brain’s effort to make sense of sparse and distorted information.","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Dreams begin with periodic bursts of spontaneous activity in the pons—the PGO waves previously described—that activate parts of the cortex.","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The cortex combines this haphazard input with whatever other activity was already occurring and does its","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"best to synthesize a story that makes sense of the information .","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Consider how this theory handles a couple of common dreams.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Your brain in its partly aroused condition feels the vestibular sensation of your position and interprets it as flying or falling.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An interpretation based on the activation-synthesis theory is that during REM sleep (which accompanies most dreams), your motor cortex is inactive and your major postural muscles are virtually paralyzed.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The main objection is that most dreams have no apparent connection to any current stimuli .","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-3-h09","text":"The Neurocognitive Model"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The neurocognitive model regards dreams as thinking that takes place under unusual conditions.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"It emphasizes that dreams begin with spontaneous brain activity related to recent memories—just as most daytime thinking relates to recent memories .","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers used a PET scan to determine which brain areas increased or decreased their activity during REM, which is correlated with dreaming.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Further, a PET scan yields a clear image only if the head remains motionless during data collection.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They also inserted a cannula (plastic tube) into each person’s arm so that they could inject radioactive chemicals during the night.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because the researchers foresaw the difficulty of sleeping under these conditions (!), they had their participants stay awake the entire previous night.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The upshot of all this is that the dreaming brain has little sensory input, leaving other brain areas free to generate images without constraints or interference.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because the primary motor cortex is suppressed and the motor areas of the spinal cord are inhibited, arousal cannot lead to action.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Activity is suppressed in the prefrontal cortex, which is important for working memory and logical thinking.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Meanwhile, activity is relatively high in part of the parietal cortex important for visuospatial perception.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The idea behind the neurocognitive approach is that arousal of parts of the cerebral cortex develops into a hallucinatory perception, with no sensory input to override it.","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A behavior can serve its function even when we do not fully understand that function.","sourcePrintedPage":287,"sourcePdfPage":305,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"bullet","text":"Nearly every species is more efficient at some times of day than at others.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h02","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299},{"type":"bullet","text":"The function of hibernation is simply to conserve energy while food is scarce.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h02","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299},{"type":"bullet","text":"Mexican cavefish have one population that lives in normal waters subject to alternations of day and night, and other populations that evolved to live in caves with no light and virtually constant temperature.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300},{"type":"bullet","text":"While male sandpipers are competing for mates above the Arctic Circle, many of them are active up to 23 hours per day for nearly three weeks, with no apparent harm to their health or alertness.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300},{"type":"bullet","text":"Seals also sleep in one hemisphere at a time when they are at sea, although they sleep in both hemispheres when they are on land.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300},{"type":"bullet","text":"Moreover, their sleep episodes last an average of only 11 seconds, with a total of less than 45 minutes per night.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300},{"type":"bullet","text":"Still, it gets little sleep, while remaining alert and performing normally on learning tasks.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":283,"sourcePdfPage":301},{"type":"bullet","text":"If the same bird is deprived of sleep during other seasons of the year, its performance suffers.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":283,"sourcePdfPage":301},{"type":"bullet","text":"If you do not get a good night’s sleep, your memory and cognition will suffer the next day.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h05","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302},{"type":"bullet","text":"Sleep also helps people reanalyze their memories: In one study, people who had just practiced a complex task were more likely to perceive a hidden rule (an “aha” experience) after a period of sleep than after a similar period of wakefulness.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h05","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302},{"type":"bullet","text":"If your brain strengthened synapses every time it learned something, without removing or weakening other synapses, the result might be runaway overactivity, or it might resemble the clutter in a room where you kept adding things without ever removing anything.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h05","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302},{"type":"bullet","text":"Rabbits, guinea pigs, and sheep sleep less and spend little time in REM.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h06","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302},{"type":"bullet","text":"Among young adults, those who sleep 9 or more hours per night have the highest percentage of REM sleep, and those who sleep 5 or fewer hours have the least percentage.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h06","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302},{"type":"bullet","text":"Another hypothesis sounds odd because we tend to imagine a glamorous role for REM sleep: David Maurice (1998) proposed that REM just shakes the eyeballs back and forth enough to get sufficient oxygen to the corneas of the eyes.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h06","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303},{"type":"bullet","text":"It also fits with the fact that individuals who spend more hours asleep devote a greater percentage of sleep to REM.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h06","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303},{"type":"bullet","text":"While you are asleep, you lie flat, unlike your posture for the rest of the day.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h08","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304},{"type":"bullet","text":"When you are dreaming, you really cannot move, you feel your lack of movement, and you dream of inability to move.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h08","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304},{"type":"bullet","text":"To overcome these difficulties, researchers in two studies persuaded young people to sleep with their heads firmly attached to masks that did not permit any movement.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h09","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304},{"type":"bullet","text":"You have a cannula in your arm and your head is locked into position.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h09","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304},{"type":"bullet","text":"Consequently, you not only forget most dreams after you awaken, but you also lose track of what has been happening within a dream, and sudden scene changes are common.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h09","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304},{"type":"bullet","text":"Remembering your dreams is not very useful (unless you plan to talk about them with your psychoanalyst), because you should not confuse dreams with reality.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h09","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304},{"type":"bullet","text":"Without minimizing how much we do understand about sleep, it is noteworthy how many basic questions remain unanswered.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h09","sourcePrintedPage":287,"sourcePdfPage":305},{"type":"bullet","text":"Our lack of knowledge about activities that occupy so much of our time underscores a point about the biology of behavior: We evolved tendencies to behave in certain ways that lead to survival and reproduction.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h09","sourcePrintedPage":287,"sourcePdfPage":305},{"type":"bullet","text":"Without minimizing how much we do understand about sleep, it is noteworthy how many basic questions remain unanswered.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h10","sourcePrintedPage":287,"sourcePdfPage":305},{"type":"bullet","text":"Our lack of knowledge about activities that occupy so much of our time underscores a point about the biology of behavior: We evolved tendencies to behave in certain ways that lead to survival and reproduction.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h10","sourcePrintedPage":287,"sourcePdfPage":305},{"type":"bullet","text":"A behavior can serve its function even when we do not fully understand that function.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h10","sourcePrintedPage":287,"sourcePdfPage":305},{"type":"bullet","text":"Even if we agreed on what is the most important function of sleep for humans today, it might not be the function for which sleep originally evolved.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299},{"type":"bullet","text":"Hibernating animals decrease their body temperature, usually maintaining it just slightly above that of the environment, but always warm enough to prevent the blood from freezing.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":281,"sourcePdfPage":299},{"type":"bullet","text":"If one of the main functions of sleep is to decrease activity at times of relative inefficiency, we might expect to find little or no sleep in species that are equally effective at all times of day.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":282,"sourcePdfPage":300},{"type":"bullet","text":"In contrast, if you learn something and then go to sleep, even a nap, your memory solidifies and may become better than it was before sleep .","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":284,"sourcePdfPage":302},{"type":"bullet","text":"According to the activation-synthesis hypothesis , a dream represents the brain’s effort to make sense of sparse and distorted information.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h07","sourcePrintedPage":285,"sourcePdfPage":303},{"type":"bullet","text":"The neurocognitive model regards dreams as thinking that takes place under unusual conditions.","headingId":"bp14-m8-3-h07","sourcePrintedPage":286,"sourcePdfPage":304}],"topicIds":["bp14-m8-3-h01","bp14-m8-3-h02","bp14-m8-3-h03","bp14-m8-3-h04","bp14-m8-3-h05","bp14-m8-3-h06","bp14-m8-3-h07","bp14-m8-3-h08","bp14-m8-3-h09","bp14-m8-3-h10"],"studySections":[{"id":"bp14-m8-3-study-1","title":"Why Proposed functions include conserving energy, supporting restoration and regulation, and contributing to learning and memory. Evidence does not require sleep to have exactly one benefit for every species. Evolution may have added several functions to an older biological pattern. The important task is to compare predictions of different explanations rather than treating one appealing story as final.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":281,"sourcePrintedEnd":290,"sourcePdfStart":299,"sourcePdfEnd":308},{"id":"bp14-m8-3-study-2","title":"Sleep and memory","text":"Some kinds of learning benefit from periods of sleep after practice. .","printedPage":282,"pdfPage":300,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":32},{"text":"Many animals that live near the North or South Pole greatly decrease sense of sparse and distorted information.","printedPage":285,"pdfPage":303,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":65},{"text":"Dreams begin with periodic bursts of spontaneous activity in the pons—the PGO waves previously described—that activate parts of the cortex.","printedPage":285,"pdfPage":303,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":66},{"text":"The cortex combines this haphazard input with whatever other activity was already occurring and does its","printedPage":285,"pdfPage":303,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":67},{"text":"best to synthesize a story that makes sense of the information .","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":68},{"text":"Consider how this theory handles a couple of common dreams.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":69},{"text":"Your brain in its partly aroused condition feels the vestibular sensation of your position and interprets it as flying or falling.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":70},{"text":"An interpretation based on the activation-synthesis theory is that during REM sleep (which accompanies most dreams), your motor cortex is inactive and your major postural muscles are virtually paralyzed.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":71},{"text":"The main objection is that most dreams have no apparent connection to any current stimuli .","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":72},{"text":"While you are asleep, you lie flat, unlike your posture for the rest of the day.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":101},{"text":"When you are dreaming, you really cannot move, you feel your lack of movement, and you dream of inability to move.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":102}],"originalFacts":8,"additionalFacts":2,"glossary":[{"term":"Activation-synthesis potentials","sourcePrintedPage":629,"sourcePdfPage":647}],"sourceBodyWordsAvailable":272,"sourceStatus":"source_explained","mdCrosscheck":"terms_present","wordCount":181},{"id":"bp14-m8-3-h09","title":"The Neurocognitive Model","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m8-3-h07","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"facts":[{"text":"The neurocognitive model regards dreams as thinking that takes place under unusual conditions.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":74},{"text":"It emphasizes that dreams begin with spontaneous brain activity related to recent memories—just as most daytime thinking relates to recent memories .","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":75},{"text":"Researchers used a PET scan to determine which brain areas increased or decreased their activity during REM, which is correlated with dreaming.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":76},{"text":"Further, a PET scan yields a clear image only if the head remains motionless during data collection.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":77},{"text":"They also inserted a cannula (plastic tube) into each person’s arm so that they could inject radioactive chemicals during the night.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":78},{"text":"Because the researchers foresaw the difficulty of sleeping under these conditions (!), they had their participants stay awake the entire previous night.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":79},{"text":"The upshot of all this is that the dreaming brain has little sensory input, leaving other brain areas free to generate images without constraints or interference.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":80},{"text":"Because the primary motor cortex is suppressed and the motor areas of the spinal cord are inhibited, arousal cannot lead to action.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":81},{"text":"Activity is suppressed in the prefrontal cortex, which is important for working memory and logical thinking.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":82},{"text":"Meanwhile, activity is relatively high in part of the parietal cortex important for visuospatial perception.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":83},{"text":"The idea behind the neurocognitive approach is that arousal of parts of the cerebral cortex develops into a hallucinatory perception, with no sensory input to override it.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":84},{"text":"A behavior can serve its function even when we do not fully understand that function.","printedPage":287,"pdfPage":305,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":85},{"text":"To overcome these difficulties, researchers in two studies persuaded young people to sleep with their heads firmly attached to masks that did not permit any movement.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":103},{"text":"You have a cannula in your arm and your head is locked into position.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":104},{"text":"Consequently, you not only forget most dreams after you awaken, but you also lose track of what has been happening within a dream, and sudden scene changes are common.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":105},{"text":"Remembering your dreams is not very useful (unless you plan to talk about them with your psychoanalyst), because you should not confuse dreams with reality.","printedPage":286,"pdfPage":304,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":106},{"text":"Without minimizing how much we do understand about sleep, it is noteworthy how many basic questions remain unanswered.","printedPage":287,"pdfPage":305,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":107},{"text":"Our lack of knowledge about activities that occupy so much of our time underscores a point about the biology of behavior: We evolved tendencies to behave in certain ways that lead to survival and
